app.name: OpenClaude
app.one_liner: An open-source coding-agent CLI that unifies diverse AI backends into a terminal-first workflow with tools, agents, MCP, and streaming output.

screens.name: Terminal Interface
screens.purpose: Primary interaction surface for prompting, tool invocation, and streaming agent output.

rust_commands.name: persist_knowledge
rust_commands.purpose: Store agent memory and context using local Orama persistence (feature-flagged).

rust_commands.name: select_model
rust_commands.purpose: Allow user to specify a model without explicitly declaring the provider, enabling provider-agnostic model selection.

rust_commands.name: validate_mcp_schema
rust_commands.purpose: Ensure MCP tool schemas include required fields like 'type' to prevent provider errors (e.g., Codex 400 failures).

mvp_plan: week 1: Add streaming output handler for terminal display
week 1: Implement unified CLI interface supporting --model without --provider
week 1: Integrate basic MCP tool calling with schema validation
week 1: Set up local Orama persistence behind feature flag
acceptance_tests: After enabling the Orama feature flag, agent interactions are persisted locally and retrievable in subsequent sessions.
Given a user runs `openclaude --model gpt-4o`, the system selects the appropriate OpenAI-compatible provider without requiring explicit --provider.
The terminal interface streams agent output incrementally while counting tokens with caching for performance.
When a Codex provider is used with an MCP tool missing the 'type' field, the system validates the schema and returns a clear error before sending the request.
